First, benchmark fit: every Series A-B row in the table is built from SaaS, consumer-internet and quick-commerce companies, while Carrum is an asset-heavy vehicle-leasing operator whose cost base is cars and driver payouts, not salaries. If it prices corporate ops staff against the listed-logistics market instead (Delhivery Executive Rs 2.0-4.3 LPA, Rapido Business Ops Executive Rs 2.4-4.5 LPA), real entry offers could land at Rs 3-5 LPA — below my floor. Second, Carrum may simply not hire at 0-1 yrs on the business side: every corporate posting the research surfaced specifies real experience (Program Manager 5-6 yrs, Product Manager 2-4 yrs, a Business Head, a Debt & Treasury Manager), the AI Evangelist's 0-3 window is the sole exception, and a ~150-person corporate team scaling a fleet 2x in 12 months often prefers laterals who need no training. Third, the profile records no headcount target and no hiring number anywhere in the reporting — TechCrunch says only that the company will 'hire as it scales' — so the volume and timing of every role I marked 'likely' or 'possible' is inference from what the round funds, not from anything Carrum has announced. Also note the round is small in absolute terms ($10M against a fleet-financing need for ~6,000 vehicles), which implies most of the capital goes to debt-backed asset purchase rather than payroll, and that Uber as the sole investor gives one customer unusual leverage over the cost structure.

companies.caveat: The honest problem is that nothing here is confirmed by a KARAM job posting. Three specific ways this could be wrong. (1) Zero verified openings: karam.in/careers is only a generic interest form with no listings, LinkedIn shows no KARAM-posted jobs, and the real job board at careers.karam.in failed DNS resolution from this environment (ENOTFOUND) — search snippets referenced positions in Kolkata, Panvel, Bahadurgarh, Vadodara, Dubai and Lucknow, but no titles or bands could be loaded, so every role above is inferred from what the business needs, not from a posting. Re-check careers.karam.in from an unblocked network before acting on this. (2) The round funds M&A, not hiring: the coverage quotes zero headcount targets and earmarks the capital for acquisitions, capacity, distribution and governance. Hiring here follows acquisition integration on a 6-18 month lag, so the timing could easily slip past a 2026/2027 graduation date, and the roles that open may be absorbed into an acquired company's payroll rather than KARAM's. (3) Candidate-profile mismatch: a PPE manufacturer's field sales force is often hired as diploma-holders, B.Sc/BBA graduates or industrial-safety diploma candidates rather than B.Tech graduates, and at 2.8-3.5 LPA in tier-2 plant towns — below my floor. Conversely, if KARAM does run a structured Graduate Engineer Trainee programme benchmarked against larger UP/Uttarakhand manufacturers, a Noida corporate-office offer could reach 8-9 LPA, above my ceiling. Finally, no salary aggregator carries a usable KARAM-specific entry-level sample, so this band is peer-derived throughout. Practical move given the weak signal: approach CHRO Kavita Nigam directly rather than applying through the form.

companies.caveat: The single biggest risk is that none of the forecast roles ever gets posted. QNu's live board has 18 reqs and not one entry-level seat of any kind — the four non-engineering roles are 3-10 years, and a 2016-vintage, ~140-person hardware company that has hired exclusively experienced people for a decade may simply have no graduate business rung. Second, the benchmark rows are built almost wholly from consumer internet and SaaS companies; a quantum-security hardware firm with multi-year government procurement cycles typically pays its business side more conservatively, so the band could sit 1-2 LPA high in practice — the floor is likelier than the ceiling. Third, the stage label is genuinely ambiguous: "Series A1" with Rs 375 Cr raised over ten years behaves like Series B/C on capital while the business org is seed-thin; if you price it off the Series C+ metro BD row instead, the band moves up to roughly Rs 6.5-12L fixed. Fourth, and most likely to matter for an engineering graduate specifically: if QNu hires you into a customer-facing ENGINEERING title (Application Engineer, Field/Deployment Engineer, Solutions Engineer) rather than a business title, you are paid off the engineering band, which at a funded Bengaluru deep-tech hardware company runs materially higher than anything in this table. The title on the offer letter, not the actual work, decides the number — so push for the engineering-coded title if the work is the same. Finally, the board was last updated 2026-07-27 and the round closed 2026-09-09, so everything post-raise is unobserved; re-check the greytHR feed directly (qnulabs.com/careers only redirects, the zohorecruit board is dead, and Uplers' listing is wrong on both funding and role count).

companies.fit_reason: The volume argument is real: headcount went from roughly 338 in May 2025 to about 633 by July 2026, retail registrations tripled year-on-year, and the stated plan is to take the dealer network from ~120 outlets to 500. You cannot quadruple a dealer network without hiring a lot of junior territory sales, dealer-development and after-sales people, and OEMs fill those seats with fresh graduates because the work is legwork, not judgment. So openings will exist. What makes this mixed rather than good is the shape of them. All three roles visible today ask for experience — 2-6 years, 1-5 years, 1-3 years — and none is a fresher req. There is no campus programme, no careers page and no graduate track to apply to; hiring runs through LinkedIn and Indian job boards, which favours the lateral hire with two years at Bajaj or Ather over a 2026 B.E. graduate. And the business-track entry point here is a field or plant job in a tier-2 posting at Rs 3-6L, not an HQ analyst desk — a graduate benchmarking against a Series C+ software offer will find this well below it. The honest read: strong odds of getting hired, modest pay, and the roles are closer to the mechanical/production and channel side of an auto company than to the analytics-and-strategy work "business track" usually implies. Best route in is the Chakan plant supply-chain and planning side, where a mechanical or production engineering degree is actually the qualification rather than a nice-to-have.
companies.caveat: Three things could make this wrong. First, there is no first-party careers page — bgauss.com/careers and /career both 404, and Naukri, Indeed, Glassdoor, Foundit and Shine all blocked the scrape — so the "listed now" set is three third-party listings and is a floor, not a picture; BGauss may already be running fresher intake I cannot see. Second, the stage label is doing damage: the benchmark's "Series C+" rows describe VC-backed startups, while BGauss is a conglomerate subsidiary taking a promoter-funded round, and the size of my OEM haircut is judgment, not an observed BGauss offer — no BGauss salary data was reachable. Third, the error runs both ways. If RR Global extends a group campus MT programme to BGauss's Pune HQ, corporate trainee offers could sit at Rs 6-9L, above everything I have listed. If instead the 120-to-500 dealer push is staffed the way two-wheeler OEMs usually staff it, real offers land at Rs 2.5-3.5L fixed with most upside in monthly retail incentive, below my low ends. Every band assumes the graduate is willing to take a field or plant role in a tier-2 posting.

companies.fit_reason: Mixed, and the two halves point in opposite directions. In favour: this is genuinely a company that hires 0-1 year graduates — a 15-person B2B marketplace staffs supplier calling, RFQ follow-up, catalogue building and agency delivery with freshers because that is what it can afford, and there is a real live product (the marketplace app is up and functioning) rather than a pitch deck. A graduate joining now would touch trade operations, sales and category work directly and report to a founder, which is real early exposure. Against: there is no careers page, no campus process and no listing anywhere, so hiring runs entirely through the founder's network and a cold applicant has no route in except a direct LinkedIn approach to Manav Dahuja or Kashish Goyal. Pay sits at the bottom of the seed band, ₹3.5-6L fixed, with a heavy incentive component in the sales seats. And the runway maths is unforgiving: ₹1 crore against a 15-25 person payroll is roughly 6-12 months of cover unless the GMV genuinely converts to revenue, so an offer carries employment risk a Series A company's would not. For an engineering graduate specifically, none of these roles use the degree — they are calling, Excel and documentation seats. Worth taking as a first job if it is the offer in hand and you have met the founder; not worth choosing over a structured programme at a larger employer.

companies.caveat: The honest reason this could be wrong is that it may describe hiring that never happens. Every role here is predicted, not observed — there is no careers page to check against, and a ₹1 crore raise may fund nothing beyond the founders' own runway and a contractor or two. Beyond that: (1) the stage label overstates the company — a ₹1 crore round selling ~3%, fourteen months after incorporation, from unnamed anchor investors, is angel money dressed as an institutional seed, so even the floor of the seed benchmark row may sit above what they actually pay; a ₹3L offer here would not be an anomaly. (2) Every operating claim is company-issued and unaudited: the ₹6.30 crore GMV, the 25x growth and the eight-country footprint all trace to an ANI-syndicated advertorial (The Tribune carries an explicit no-responsibility disclaimer), a StartupTalky piece, and a Dealroom page that now 404s. No independent journalism exists. If the GMV figure is soft, the trade-operations role in particular does not exist. (3) The metro benchmark tier may be wrong — New Palam Vihar is fringe Gurugram and there is a Panipat office; if hiring lands there, subtract 15-30% from every band. (4) Headcount is unverified: LinkedIn self-declares 11-50 but surfaces four employee profiles, and if the real number is closer to eight, they are hiring one or two people total, not five. (5) The profile was deliberately left unverified, which is why band_confidence is dropped a step to low. Separately, do not merge this with "Baba", the US patient-advocacy startup that raised $6.5M led by General Catalyst in February 2026 — different company, different continent.

companies.fit_reason:
OSM will hire 2026/27 graduates, but mostly not into the roles a business-track candidate is imagining. All five live listings are mid-to-senior - an AGM/DGM/GM, an Assistant Manager/Sr. EHS Officer, two Territory Sales Managers and an Area Sales Manager - and none is a 0-1 year requisition. There is no named management trainee or graduate leadership programme, which is what a 350-700 person manufacturer would need for structured fresher intake; at this size, junior hiring is requisition-by-requisition through Naukri and referrals.

What genuinely works in a fresher's favour: the round funds dealer network expansion from ~150 to 250 touchpoints by FY28, and that is manpower-hungry, junior-heavy work - dealer onboarding, field sales support, service desks - that OEMs staff with fresh graduates because the volume is high and the pay is low. A mechanical or electrical graduate also has a clean shot at plant-side sourcing and service seats. What works against: this is a plant-heavy engineering business where the prestige track is GET/technical, not business; the business-track pay is manufacturer-grade Rs 3.5-6L, roughly half what a funded consumer-tech firm pays a business associate in Gurugram; the work is travel-intensive and tier-2/3 based; and anyone hoping for product, growth, category or analytics work will not find it - OSM has no such function at fresher level. Rated mixed rather than good because the doors that exist are narrow and low-paid, and mixed rather than poor because unlike a bank NBFC or a 30-year-old industrial house, OSM has a concrete, funded, headcount-creating expansion underway right now.
companies.caveat: Four honest reasons this could be wrong. (1) The careers page is stale - its five posts are dated July 2024, so it both understates real hiring and gives me no live fresher requisition to anchor on; every predicted role here is inferred from the stated use of funds and the business model, not observed. companies.fit_reason: The door is genuinely open — every role Ekatra has posted is junior, three of the five are explicitly pitched at fresher level, and a company hiring ~11 people onto a ~10-30 person base will take graduates because it cannot afford anyone else. A numerate B.E. graduate has a real edge in three of these seats: performance marketing (ROAS, CAC, cohort and contribution-margin math), e-commerce catalogue and merchandising across a 5,000+ design library, and fulfilment operations on a vertically integrated chain with IGI certification, hallmarking, insured logistics and US/Middle East export documentation. That last one is closer to an industrial-engineering problem than most people expect. Against that: there is no engineering organisation here at all and no prospect of one, so the degree is credential-only; the money is Rs 3-6.5L for most of these roles, at or below the median Indian fresher offer; a six-month-old brand with no HR function offers no structured training, no rotation and no graduate programme, so the learning is entirely self-directed and the manager is likely a founder; equity is effectively nil; and one of the likeliest openings is a shop-floor client-advisor job that a B.E. graduate would be overqualified for and that rarely converts into a business-track career. This is a good first job for someone who specifically wants D2C consumer-brand operating experience in Mumbai and is willing to trade pay and stability for scope. For anyone else it is a poor risk-adjusted choice.
companies.caveat: Four things could make this wrong. First, the role list is the weak link: it comes from a single LinkedIn hiring post roughly a month old, and one retrieval of the jobs page flagged it as past/archived with nothing confirmed live — so "listed now" means "was posted verbatim", not "open today", and anyone acting on this should email info@ekatrajewels.com before treating any title as real. Second, no benchmark row in the file has a jewellery, luxury or physical-retail cut; every row I used is built from tech-startup and e-commerce salary data, and luxury retail conventionally pays client-facing staff less fixed and more variable than these bands imply, so the split between my band and an actual offer could be structural rather than a level difference. Third, no Ekatra salary has ever been reported to any aggregator, headcount is a self-reported LinkedIn 2-10 band, and the cap table is celebrity/strategic (Ekta Kapoor, Sussanne Khan, Sanjay Kapoor) rather than institutional — that register can support either an above-band brand-building splurge or a deliberately thin cash payroll, and I cannot tell which from outside. Fourth, the company is six months old with a Rs 10 Cr round; a single retail-expansion decision could double or halt this entire hiring plan before any of these roles reach a graduate.

companies.fit_reason: Genuinely two-sided. In favour: the Indian water and wastewater treatment industry is one of the few sectors that routinely hires fresh B.Tech graduates straight into commercial seats — sales engineer, proposals and estimation, service coordination — because the product needs someone who can read a P&ID and size a plant, and a chemical, environmental, mechanical or civil graduate from 2026/2027 is precisely that candidate. A 5-person company also gives a fresher exposure to the whole cycle, from enquiry to commissioning to AMC, that a large EPC firm would not. Against, and this is the part that keeps it out of "good": there is no careers page, no LinkedIn job, no HR function and no evidence of any hiring at all — the empty currently_open list is real, not a research gap. The first two or three hires at a company like this are far more likely to be an experienced process-design engineer and a proven NCR sales person with an existing builder and consultant network than a fresher, because a pre-seed team cannot afford to train. Realistically, treat this as a company to watch and approach directly rather than one to plan around. There is no campus process, no structured programme and no guarantee it hires anyone this financial year. Pay will be below what a peer of yours gets at a funded software startup, and the honest offset is ownership and hands-on scope, not cash.

companies.caveat:
The honest reason this could be wrong: every role here is predicted, none is observed. The company has published zero job listings, so the role list is inferred from what the round is stated to fund and from how comparable Indian water-treatment businesses staff up — if the founders instead spend the next year on product validation and the factory with no commercial hires at all, the correct answer for a 2026/2027 graduate is that there is nothing here, and that outcome is entirely plausible for a three-month-old company with Rs 1 lakh paid-up capital and an undisclosed round.

Three more specific failure modes. First, the round size is undisclosed. Pre-seed from one angel could be Rs 50 lakh or Rs 5 crore, and those imply very different pay envelopes; I banded for the small end, so if the cheque was large every number here is 20-30% low. Second, the sector haircut is my judgment, not a benchmark row — the file has no water, cleantech or industrial-equipment family, so I mapped a hardware EPC business onto rows built from software-startup postings and cut them. A reader who thinks a VC-backed "productised STP" company will pay like a tech startup would land closer to Rs 4.5-7L for the sales seat. Third, small industrial firms in Delhi NCR often hire freshers as six-month unpaid or stipendiary trainees (Rs 10,000-20,000/month) before confirming a CTC at all, which would put a real first-year number below the bottom of every band above.

Band confidence is set to low deliberately: the strongest underlying row was only medium, and all three lowering conditions in the rules apply at once — the company is very small (2-5 people), the stage label is contested (export says Seed, all coverage says pre-seed), and the profile is unverified because no careers page or listing exists to check against. companies.fit_reason: Mixed, and the two halves pull hard in opposite directions. Against: not one of the five currently-open roles is a fresher role. Operations Head, Manager - B2B Enterprise Sales (4-6 yrs), Purchase Executive (2-4 yrs) and Warehouse Manager Pune (2-5 yrs) all demand experience, there is no careers page, no campus programme, and no management-trainee track - at 17-30 people on the core payroll, every hire has to be productive in week one, and a company that has just raised for asset purchases rather than headcount has little slack to train anyone. The only open role a 0-1 year candidate clears outright is the Bahadrabad Warehouse Supervisor at Rs 1.8-3.6 LPA, which is a shift-floor job in a small Uttarakhand town, not a business-track launchpad. For: the underlying work is unusually well matched to a mechanical, industrial, production or civil graduate in a way that a fintech or SaaS seed never is. Pooling operations is physical-flow problem solving - cycle time, dwell time, asset recovery rates, wash-line throughput, reverse-logistics routing - and B.Tech grads with no MBA are the standard hire for it across Indian logistics and 3PL companies. An eight-depot network expanding on fresh capital creates junior ops and depot seats faster than it creates senior ones, and joining a 20-person company at seed means real scope within a year. The honest read: apply for the ops and depot track and expect Rs 3.5-6 LPA in Gurugram or Rs 2.5-4.5 LPA at a cluster site, treat enterprise sales and founder's office as long shots until they post them, and be aware that nothing on their board today is aimed at you.
companies.caveat: The honest reason this could be wrong is that six of the eight roles are inferred from what the round funds, not observed anywhere - and this company has given no signal at all that it hires freshers into business roles. Every posting it has made asks for 2-6 years. If Yantra Packs simply keeps hiring experienced operators, as most 20-person asset-heavy companies do, the correct answer is closer to "poor fit, one warehouse job" than to the eight-role list above. Specific weaknesses: (a) yantrapacks.com has no careers section - /careers and /career both 404, there is no sitemap - so the role list is a best-effort union scraped across LinkedIn, Naukri, Glassdoor and Indeed, and the Purchase Executive and Pune Warehouse Manager entries come from search-result summaries rather than pages anyone opened, since Naukri and Glassdoor both returned 403; the Pune listing dates to June 2026 and may well be filled. (b) The benchmark rows carrying most of the weight here are the weakest in the file - the ops/supply-chain seed rows and the business-analyst seed rows are all marked low confidence and are explicitly described by their own notes as triangulated or extrapolated rather than measured, because no Indian salary aggregator tags employers by funding stage. (c) Rs 12 Cr goes much less far here than at a software seed: the capital is earmarked for containers, warehouses and the Trakkia stack, so the headcount plan behind this round may be a handful of hires rather than the dozen this list implies, and the ones that happen may skew senior. (d) Band confidence is set to low, one step below what the source rows would otherwise support, because a 17-person payroll is small enough that any single founder's preference moves an offer more than the market does. (e) Watch the name when searching: the legal entity is Yantraksh Logistics Private Limited and most boards file it that way, while "Yantra" plus recruitment overwhelmingly returns Yantra India Limited, the Ministry of Defence ammunition PSU with thousands of apprentice vacancies - a completely unrelated employer.

companies.fit_reason: Accessible but badly matched — those are two separate findings and both are real. On accessibility: this company will hire hundreds of 0-1 year people over the next 12 months, because 171 work-in-progress gold branches cannot open without them, and Loan Officer and Operations Executive are genuine no-experience-required rungs. A 2026/27 graduate who applies will get looked at. On match: six of the nine posted roles (Cluster Manager, Operations Manager, Regional Manager, Zonal Manager, Team Lead Sales, Insurance Manager) are 3-15 year branch-banking seats a fresher cannot reach, so the real fresher surface is two or three titles. Those titles are field jobs in tier-3 towns across AP, Telangana, Karnataka and Odisha — Dharmavaram, Adoni, Kavali, Podili, Nizamabad — not Hyderabad HO, and they effectively require Telugu or Kannada. They pay ₹2-3.5L against roughly ₹3.5-4.5L for a mass IT-services offer, with a large slice contingent on disbursement targets and no equity to compensate. And the profile's most telling detail is the absence: zero engineering roles posted despite ICRA explicitly flagging that Keertana must keep augmenting its IT systems, which means an engineering degree buys essentially no premium here and no technical career track. Worth applying to if the candidate wants NBFC branch-lending experience, is regionally rooted, and values a fast-scaling lender where branch managers get made early — a strong Loan Officer can be running a branch in 24-36 months in a network growing this fast. Not worth it as a default fallback offer for someone with an IT-services or GCC option open.
companies.caveat: Four honest reasons this could be wrong. First, the careers page is not a job board — it is an application form with a "Position Applying" dropdown, so those nine entries are the options the form accepts, not nine dated live requisitions. Some may be evergreen and some stale; treat none of them as a confirmed open mandate without calling HO. Second, no benchmark row in the file covers gold-loan NBFC branch roles. Every band here is transposed from adjacent field-sales, warehouse-ops and bank-MT populations, and the closest true comparables — Muthoot Finance and Manappuram junior relationship executives in the same AP/Telangana geography — are not in the dataset and were not fetched in this session, so the field bands rest on inference rather than on matched observations. Third, the stage bucket is genuinely ambiguous and the two candidate rows disagree by roughly 2x at the top: the profile itself flags that "Series B" is a database label and that the company should be paid as a mid-size BFSI employer, which means the honest answer sits between the Series C+ and listed/large rows rather than on either. I leaned toward the branch-network reading, and if Keertana instead pays like a funded growth-stage lender competing for talent, the HO bands in particular are 20-30% low. Fourth, and most likely to invalidate the predicted roles specifically: high-volume NBFC branch hiring in tier-3 towns overwhelmingly runs through walk-in drives, regional consultants and employee referrals that never touch the corporate careers page. The four predicted roles may exist as real needs and still never appear as a postable fresher requisition — and conversely, the fresher intake for the 171 new branches may already be flowing entirely through channels this analysis cannot see.

companies.fit_reason: They genuinely do hire freshers into business roles — the two WorkIndia listings loaded today say "graduate/fresher" in as many words, so unlike many industrial SMEs this is not a closed door. But the pay is the problem, not the access: ₹15,000-21,000/month is roughly ₹1.8-2.5 LPA, below the benchmark floor for almost every entry-level business family in India, and there is no structured management-trainee or graduate programme to compensate. For a 2026/27 B.E. graduate specifically, the honest read is that the better door at this company is the technical one — a mechanical, chemical, electrical or instrumentation graduate is a far stronger candidate for the field-service engineer, applications engineer and R&D roles the ₹30 Cr round is actually funding (miniaturised fluid treatment, fleet automation, re-refining), and those roles are simply not visible on any public board yet. The business track here is a fine entry point for domain learning in industrial B2B and lubrication/circularity, and the customer list is genuinely blue-chip experience, but a graduate optimising for first-year cash should treat these bands as a floor to negotiate off, not a target.

companies.caveat: The careers data underneath this is thin and partly stale, which is the biggest single risk. Only the three WorkIndia sales listings were actually loaded and read today; the HR Generalist, Accounts Executive, Sr. Project Management Officer, Marketing Head and Senior Graphic Designer entries come from captcha-blocked Naukri/Jobaaj/Glassdoor pages read as search-index snippets, with posting dates spanning Nov 2025 to Apr 2026 — several may be closed. Minimac has no functioning careers page and its LinkedIn jobs tab was empty, so there is no clean same-day snapshot to check against. Second risk: the ₹30 Cr round closed only four weeks ago (2026-08-12) and every observed salary point predates it or barely postdates it, so if the company resets its pay structure to compete for regional-hub and R&D talent, the sales bands here could be 30-50% low within a year — my bands describe the Minimac that existed before the money landed. Third: the stage label is genuinely ambiguous and the benchmark rows I used are the weakest in the file (every seed x non-metro row is self-flagged "low confidence" and extrapolated rather than measured), so the row itself may be wrong in the same direction I am. Finally, all ten roles are inferred to be non-engineering, which is itself odd for a company whose round funds R&D — if Minimac's actual post-round hiring turns out to be overwhelmingly technical, the business-track list here will look larger than reality.

A 26-person company cannot have two marketing heads and nobody below them building audiences, uploading creatives and pulling Meta/Google reports - the junior paid-media seat is the standard first hire under a D2C marketing head, and it is the one seat here a 0-1 year candidate is genuinely hired into.

estimated_roles.title: Ecommerce / Marketplace Operations Executive
estimated_roles.family: Category management and merchandising
estimated_roles.why: 'Ecommerce Manager' is open now (posted 2 days ago). A physical toy sold direct plus almost certainly on Amazon/Flipkart/FirstCry needs someone doing listings, catalogue copy, A+ content, pricing updates, stock sync and returns reconciliation - the executor layer under that manager. Character story cards and books mean an expanding SKU count, which is exactly what creates this seat.

estimated_roles.title: Fulfilment & Supply Chain Executive
estimated_roles.family: Operations, supply chain and city launch (entry-level, 0-2 years, India)
estimated_roles.why: The round funds 'scaling manufacturing in India' and a 'Warehouse Manager' is already listed. Consumer hardware at seed means inbound from a contract manufacturer, inventory counts, courier/3PL coordination, RTO handling and warranty returns (the site carries a warranty policy). That manager will need one or two junior hands, and this is the role where an engineering graduate's background is an actual advantage rather than a mismatch.

estimated_roles.title: Content & Social Media Associate
estimated_roles.family: Growth and performance marketing (content/social sub-band, below paid media)
estimated_roles.why: 'Creative and Content Lead' was posted hours ago, and the round funds broadening the catalogue of characters, languages and original content plus 'Wippi Radio'. A kids' brand selling to parents lives on Instagram, YouTube Shorts and parent WhatsApp communities, which is high-volume production work a lead cannot do alone. Note this seat competes with agencies and mass-communication graduates, so an engineering grad needs a real portfolio to win it.

estimated_roles.title: Founder's Office / Business Associate
estimated_roles.family: Founder's office / chief of staff / strategy associate - entry-level (0-2 years), India
estimated_roles.why: Two founders, a first institutional round, and a stated 12-month commercial target is the classic trigger for a founder's-office hire who chases cohort/retention numbers, investor reporting and whatever is on fire that week. Marked 'possible' rather than 'likely' because at a $1.2M round this seat often stays unfilled or goes to an intern, and when it is filled it is usually a tier-1 campus hire.

estimated_roles.title: Customer Experience Associate (parent support and warranty)
estimated_roles.family: Operations, supply chain and city launch (support sub-band; no dedicated support row in the benchmarks)
estimated_roles.why: A screen-free device in the hands of a 4-10 year old generates setup calls, pairing problems, damaged-card replacements and warranty claims from anxious parents. As units ship at scale this stops being something the founders answer on WhatsApp. Lowest-paid seat on this list and the least career-forming for an engineering graduate, so it is listed for completeness, not as a recommendation.

companies.fit_reason: Mixed, and the reason is a timing mismatch rather than a policy against freshers. What works: a 26-person seed D2C brand in Bengaluru that just raised for demand generation and fulfilment genuinely does hire cheap junior execution - someone to run the ad accounts, load the catalogue, pack and track the boxes, answer the parents. Those are real entry-level seats and the money for them is in the round. What does not work: every one of the six roles open today is a lead, head or manager title - Creative and Content Lead, Ecommerce Manager, Product Growth Manager (D2C), Head of Marketing, Head of Digital Marketing, Warehouse Manager. Not one is entry-level, so a 2026/2027 graduate applying this week has nothing to apply to on the business track. The junior seats above are the layer that gets hired three to six months after those leads land, which points at late 2026 into 2027 rather than now. Two further frictions for an engineering graduate specifically. First, these business roles are contested by commerce, communications and BBA graduates who look more natural on paper for catalogue, content and support work; the fulfilment/supply-chain seat is the one where an engineering degree reads as an asset. Second, Wippi is hiring engineers directly - Embedded Software Engineer (listed twice) and a Testing & Quality Engineer Intern - so an engineering graduate's highest-probability route into this company is the technical track, not the business track. A practical note: there is no careers page on wippi.com and no structured graduate programme at 26 people, so entry-level hiring here happens through the founders' networks, LinkedIn DMs and internships that convert. A cold application to a job board is the weakest available channel.
companies.caveat: The honest reason this could be wrong: no role on this list is actually posted. Every one of the six roles Wippi has live is a lead or manager title, so all six bands here are predictions about a hiring layer that does not exist yet, priced off benchmark rows that no source tags by funding stage - the seed-stage cut in every row I used is the benchmark author's inference from company names, not observed seed offers. Three specific ways this breaks. First, a 26-person hardware company may simply never open these seats: the standard move at $1.2M is to hire one experienced generalist who does catalogue, ads and fulfilment together, or to outsource the whole layer to a D2C growth agency and a 3PL, in which case the correct answer for a fresher is zero roles rather than six. Second, the confidence rating is low for a reason - the category, ops and business-analyst rows are all self-described as low-confidence extrapolations, and I lowered a step further for headcount, so individual offers here will vary more than these bands do; a founder who wants a specific person will pay outside them in either direction. Third, four of the six live roles came from an aggregator mirror rather than LinkedIn directly and may already be filled, which would change what the junior layer under them looks like. One more thing worth knowing before any conversation with them: wippi.com advertises '59,000+ families' while the funding coverage frames 15,000 families as a forward target - those cannot both be current customers, so do not quote either figure back to them as traction, and read the site number as marketing reach.

estimated_roles.family: Product analyst and associate product manager (APM)
estimated_roles.why: Maps to the one genuinely new product line the round funds: the AI Contact Centre plus automated evaluation platform. estimated_roles.family: Business development, inside sales and account management
estimated_roles.why: One Enterprise Sales Manager and one Account Manager cannot generate their own pipeline across the entire Indian BFSI universe. The standard next GTM hire after a Series A with an enterprise-expansion mandate is an SDR/BDR to build and work the bank/NBFC/insurer outbound list and qualify inbound from the funding coverage. This is the most realistic genuine entry-level business door at Navana over the next 12 months.

estimated_roles.family: Pre-sales and solutions engineering (business-side technical GTM)
estimated_roles.why: On-premise deployment inside regulated BFSI means every deal runs through a POC, a security and compliance review and integration scoping against a bank's telephony and core systems. That work sits between sales and engineering and is the standard way an early-stage deep-tech company scales deployments without adding expensive senior sellers. Best-fit seat on this list for a 2026/27 engineering graduate, because the qualification is being able to wire up an STT/TTS API and explain a WER number to a bank's IT team.

estimated_roles.family: Operations, supply chain and city launch (customer operations)
estimated_roles.why: 100M+ voice minutes are already live at named regulated clients, and the round funds deeper penetration of those same accounts. estimated_roles.why: The second use of funds is to "strengthen its speech models for Indian languages and dialects" - currently 12 languages and 40-45 dialects. Before that is a modelling problem it is a data-sourcing and label-quality problem: recruiting speakers, managing transcription vendors, auditing per-dialect label quality, and building evaluation sets. Historically the most fresher-accessible non-engineering seat at an Indian speech company, and it scales headcount cheaply, which suits a Rs 40 crore round.

estimated_roles.title: Associate Product Manager / Product Analyst (AI Contact Centre & evaluation platform)
estimated_roles.family: Product analyst and associate product manager (APM)
estimated_roles.why: The automated evaluation platform is inherently metric-driven - call QA scores, accuracy by language and dialect, containment and deflection rates - which usually pulls in an analyst once the first enterprise customers are live. Marked possible rather than likely because at 25-45 people this work is normally loaded onto the senior PM they are already hiring; an APM seat only appears if the contact-centre line gets traction fast.

estimated_roles.title: Founder's Office / Business Associate
estimated_roles.family: Founder's office / chief of staff / strategy associate
estimated_roles.why: Two founder-brothers with fresh institutional capital and new investor reporting obligations to Screwvala, Antler India and three angels is the classic trigger for a founder's-office hire. Marked possible only: the careers page currently shows zero appetite for general org build-out - no growth, strategy, category or operations roles - and the reporting quotes no headcount target, so this would be opportunistic rather than planned.

companies.caveat: The strongest reason this estimate could be wrong is that Navana currently has no entry-level door at all. All six live roles are Manager or Senior titles (Account Manager, Enterprise Sales Manager, Product Manager, Product Designer, Senior MLOps Engineer, DevSecOps Engineer), and the funding coverage quotes no hiring plan, no headcount target and no new-city or international expansion - the only forward-looking language is the three use-of-funds phrases. Every "likely" and "possible" role above is my inference from what the round funds, not something Navana has announced, and a capital-efficient company that took eight years to reach a Rs 40 crore Series A may spend it on a handful of experienced GTM and infra people rather than building a junior funnel at all. Three further sources of error: headcount is a LinkedIn band estimate (11-50), not a published figure, so the company could be materially smaller than assumed and pay accordingly; remote-first hiring means comp may be set on a national rather than a Mumbai band, which would push a non-metro candidate 25-35% below the row I used; and at this size founders set compensation by discretion and candidate-by-candidate negotiation, so a single strong technical grad who can demo voice-AI work could be offered well above 9 LPA while a generic business hire could be offered 4-5. Finally, the benchmark row itself is medium confidence and stage-attributed by inference - no Indian salary source segments employers by funding stage - and I lowered it a further step for company size, so treat 5-9 as a planning bracket for a conversation, not a number to reject an offer on.

salary_benchmarks.family: Product analyst and associate product manager (entry-level, 0-2 years, India)

bands.note: Thinnest data of any row - no source I could reach breaks out pre-Series A separately. Built bottom-up: Payscale India Product Analyst averages Rs 5.12L for <1 yr and Rs 7.84L for 1-4 yrs (76 profiles, Jul 2026); Talent.com puts entry Product Analyst at Rs 8.0L. Then applied the only published early-stage adjustment I found - productmanagementjob.com's 'pre-seed to Series A: below market, often 10-25% under the national median, highest equity percentage' - to the Rs 12L median entry APM base. In practice product-analyst titles cluster Rs 6-9L here and APM titles Rs 10-14L. Variable is usually token (0-10%) at this stage; the gap between Rs 14L fixed and Rs 20L total is almost entirely ESOP notional, which is a large percentage of a tiny cap table - treat it as paper, not pay. Confidence low: extrapolated from stage-discount language, not from observed seed-stage offers.

Genuinely no direct data for this combination - I could not find a single source reporting seed-stage entry-level product pay outside the metros. Derived by applying the published non-metro adjustment (Davzon India Salary Guide 2026: 0.82x tier-2 multiplier, 0.75x for remote/tier-3; Beacon Filing: 'tier 2 cities typically run 15-30% below tier 1 equivalents') to the metro seed row, with the floor cross-checked against Payscale's 10th percentile of Rs 3.44L for Product Analyst India-wide and Davzon's junior business analyst band of Rs 4-7L. Confidence low and should be treated as a rough prior only - at this stage and location, individual offers vary far more than any band, and equity terms matter more than the cash number.

Best-supported startup row. Four independent write-ups converge: Product Leadership puts growth-stage startup APMs at Rs 12-22L, 'ESOP heavy', and its calculator returns Rs 12-16L base + Rs 2-4L variable + Rs 2-6L ESOP for a Series B+ mid-size entry PM; productmanagementjob.com gives entry APM base Rs 9-16.2L, median Rs 12L, total comp Rs 13.4L, with Series B-D 'at or slightly above median' plus 'meaningful options'; Recrew gives entry APM Rs 8-15L with a 0-2 yr average of Rs 15L. The Rs 8L low end is the product-analyst title (and analytics-flavoured APM roles), not a branded APM program. Bonus convention is 10-20% of base. Confidence medium rather than high because every source states company stage qualitatively and the LPA figures are not themselves cut by funding stage.

Series A-B companies outside Bengaluru/Gurugram/Mumbai are concentrated in Pune, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, Chennai, Jaipur and Indore. Band derived by applying the tier-2 adjustment (Davzon 0.82x; Beacon Filing 15-30% below tier-1) to the metro Series A-B row. Directionally consistent with Indeed India's non-metro APM city averages (Hyderabad Rs 13.04L, Chennai Rs 13.02L, Noida Rs 12.51L) and with OnJob's statement that Hyderabad and Pune typically run 5-15% below Bengaluru - but those Indeed figures are all-experience averages, not filtered to 0-2 years, so they over-read the entry band. Confidence low: the adjustment is real and published, the underlying stage-specific non-metro data is not.

This is where the crowdsourced data actually concentrates, because late-stage startups and unicorns are what people report. Indeed India: APM average base Rs 16.39L (25 salaries, Aug 2026), low Rs 11.71L to high Rs 22.95L, Gurgaon Rs 20.14L and Bengaluru Rs 17.04L; named late-stage employers on that page include ShareChat Rs 22.14L and Slice Rs 22.00L. OnJob puts APM (0-2 yrs) total cash at Rs 12-28L, median Rs 18L, at 'product and funded-startup companies'. 6figr's India APM page reports an average of Rs 17L (I could only read that figure from the listing, the page body did not render for me). Product-analyst titles at the same companies sit lower - Indeed's India Product Analyst average base is Rs 12.70L (23 salaries) - which is why the fixed low is Rs 12L rather than higher. Total high adds ~10-15% variable plus roughly Rs 4-8L/yr of ESOP notional. Confidence medium, not high: sample sizes on Indeed are 23-25, and the title is applied inconsistently across levels.

Anchored on actual reported non-metro city numbers rather than a multiplier: Indeed India APM averages Hyderabad Rs 13.04L, Chennai Rs 13.02L, Noida Rs 12.51L; Indeed Product Analyst averages Chennai Rs 10.13L and Hyderabad Rs 7.42L. Cross-checked against OnJob (Hyderabad/Pune typically 5-15% below Bengaluru) and Product Leadership's all-level PM city index (Delhi NCR -12%, Hyderabad -17%, Pune -28%, Chennai -33% versus Bengaluru). Caveat that keeps this at medium rather than high: those city figures are all-experience averages for a junior-skewed title, not a clean 0-2 year cut, so the true entry band is probably at the lower half of what the averages imply. ESOP at Series C+ is real but usually a smaller multiple than at Series A-B, hence the narrower fixed-to-total gap.

Deliberately the widest band because this bucket is bimodal and averaging it would mislead. Lower mode - IT services, BFSI, listed non-tech: Jobaaj cites Rs 8-12L starting packages for entry-level product roles at IT services firms; Product Leadership puts service/traditional IT APMs at Rs 8-15L; Davzon puts a junior (0-2 yr) business analyst at Rs 4-7L and a junior PM at Rs 8-14L. Upper mode - branded APM programs and big-tech/listed consumer tech: Jobaaj reports top APM programs at Google, Microsoft, Meta, Flipkart, Zepto and PhonePe paying Rs 16-45L; Product Leadership puts tier-1 product companies at Rs 18-35L with ESOPs. The Rs 45L total high assumes an RSU-heavy big-tech APM offer where stock is 30-60% of total comp (productmanagementjob.com). Note Levels.fyi India shows a PM 25th percentile of Rs 29.2L and median Rs 44.6L total, but that is all levels and is badly skewed to senior big-tech PMs - do not read it as an entry-level number. Confidence medium.

Same bimodality as the metro row, compressed at the bottom but not at the top. Lower mode: IT services and shared-services entry analyst roles in Pune, Chennai, Kolkata, Coimbatore and Indore run Rs 5-10L, consistent with Davzon's junior BA band of Rs 4-7L before its 0.82x tier-2 multiplier and Beacon Filing's 15-30% tier-2 discount (it cites a 36% Bangalore-to-Coimbatore gap for developers). Upper mode: global capability centres in Hyderabad and Pune pay at or near metro parity, which is why the high end stays at Rs 18L fixed / Rs 28L total rather than being multiplied down - Levels.fyi India business analyst city averages are Hyderabad Rs 19.58L and Pune Rs 18.66L, both above Mumbai's Rs 15.43L (all levels). Indeed's Product Analyst page lists large-employer outliers such as Amadeus Rs 19.33L and Sopra Steria Rs 19.00L. Confidence medium; read this row as two distributions, not one, and place a specific offer by employer type before city.

salary_benchmarks.family: Growth and performance marketing (entry-level, 0-2 years, India)

bands.note: Titles seed startups actually post: Growth Associate, Performance Marketing Associate/Executive, Paid Media Executive. AmbitionBox (Aug-Sep 2026 refresh): Growth Marketing Executive 0-1yr Rs4.3-4.8L, 1-3yr Rs5.1-5.6L (158 salaries); Performance Marketing Associate 0-1yr Rs2.8-4.1L, 1-3yr Rs4.7-5.7L (77); Growth Executive typical Rs4.3-4.8L (643); Growth Marketing Associate 1-3yr Rs4.0-4.4L (13, AmbitionBox itself flags medium confidence); Paid Media Executive 1-3yr Rs3.8-4.3L (353). Rs8L fixed is the realistic ceiling and needs a strong signal (tier-1 campus, prior D2C/agency internship with real ad-spend ownership, or a well-capitalised YC/Accel seed). ESOP is normal at this stage but for a 0-2yr hire the grant is small in notional terms (often 0.01-0.05%, roughly Rs0.5-1.5L/yr of paper) and should be discounted heavily - the Rs10L total-high assumes ~Rs1-1.5L notional ESOP plus a 5-10% variable. Confidence capped at medium because no source I could reach tags data by funding stage; the stage split is my inference from the title mix, not a sourced cut.

Extrapolated, not directly sourced - there is no reachable dataset that isolates seed-stage growth hires outside the metros, so treat this row as an estimate. Anchors used: AmbitionBox city cut for Digital Marketing Executive (Pune Rs3.2-3.5L, Hyderabad Rs3.3-3.7L vs Bengaluru/Mumbai Rs3.6-4.0L) and Indeed India (Digital Marketing Executive national average base Rs2.28L, 588 salaries, updated 25 May 2026; Pune Rs3.79L, Hyderabad Rs3.61L). The observed tier-2 discount at the executive band is only ~10-15%, but the seed ecosystem outside metros is thin and offers cluster low. Below roughly Rs3L this stops being a growth-marketing offer and becomes a general digital-marketing executive job. ESOP is often offered here but is close to worthless in cash terms at this stage - do not let it justify a fixed-cash number below Rs3.5L.

AmbitionBox Aug-Sep 2026: Performance Marketing Analyst 1-3yr Rs5.5-6.1L (32 salaries); Performance Marketing Associate 1-3yr Rs4.7-5.7L with reported points such as AdYogi Rs6.5L at 1yr; Marketing Associate Bengaluru Rs5.7-6.3L, Gurugram Rs5.6-6.2L, Mumbai Rs5.5-6.0L (4.4k salaries); Growth Executive Gurugram Rs5.2-6.5L; Senior Performance Marketing Executive 1-3yr Rs6.0-7.0L (371). Levels.fyi India Marketing 25th percentile total comp is Rs9.38L (verified offers, updated 10 Sep 2026) - a fair proxy for the junior end of the funded-startup sample. Rs12L fixed is the top of the band and generally requires an MBA or a demonstrated P&L/ad-spend track record. ESOP is standard and meaningful at A-B: assume Rs1.5-3L/yr notional over a 4-year vest plus a 10% variable to reach the Rs16L total-high. Medium confidence: the underlying salary counts are good, but the stage attribution is inferred.

Thin evidence - marked low deliberately. AmbitionBox city cuts show only a small tier-2 discount at associate level (Marketing Associate Pune Rs5.3-6.0L vs Bengaluru Rs5.7-6.3L; Digital Marketing Associate Pune Rs3.8-4.2L, Hyderabad Rs4.0-4.4L vs Bengaluru Rs4.0-4.5L), but Levels.fyi's aggregate city medians show a much wider gap at the funded-company end (Hyderabad Rs9.03L vs Bengaluru Rs19.83L, updated 10 Sep 2026), which is what drags this band down versus the metro row. Practically, most Series A-B companies hiring outside the metros are in Pune, Hyderabad, Chennai, Ahmedabad or Jaipur, and the sample is too small for anyone to publish a clean band. ESOP is offered on the same terms as the metro row; the discount is almost entirely in fixed cash.

This band is genuinely wide because two different hires sit in it. A non-MBA growth/performance analyst promoted in lands Rs8-13L fixed; a tier-1 MBA or premium campus growth hire lands Rs14-18L, occasionally Rs20L+. Evidence (AmbitionBox, Aug-Sep 2026): Growth Manager India 1-3yr Rs12.9-14.3L (553 salaries in that bucket, 3.2k overall); Growth Marketing Manager 1-3yr Rs11.8-15.2L (915); Performance Marketing Manager 1-3yr Rs8.5-10.4L (2.8k). Company pages: PhonePe growth manager Rs11.5-17.1L for 2-7yrs (30 salaries, AmbitionBox high confidence), Unacademy Rs11.6-15.6L for 1-8yrs (34, high confidence), Zepto 1-3yr estimated Rs12.8-18.9L, Razorpay 1-3yr estimated Rs13.6-19.4L, Groww 3-6yr Rs19.7-29.5L. City premium is real: Growth Manager Bengaluru Rs17.1-18.9L, Gurugram Rs16.6-18.5L, Mumbai Rs15.6-18.0L. Total-high of Rs26L assumes 15-20% variable plus Rs3-6L/yr notional ESOP - and at C+ that ESOP is worth more than at earlier stages because secondaries and buybacks are common. Note the 'Manager' title inflation: many of these 1-3yr datapoints are post-MBA, so a 0-2yr non-MBA candidate should anchor to the lower half.

Low confidence: very few Series C+ companies run growth teams outside Bengaluru/Gurugram/Mumbai, so no source publishes this cut and I am extrapolating. Anchors: AmbitionBox Growth Manager Noida Rs14.2-17.4L and New Delhi Rs15.1-17.0L versus Bengaluru Rs17.1-18.9L (a ~10-20% step down for near-metro NCR, and the step is steeper for true tier-2); Performance Marketing Manager New Delhi Rs12.9-14.2L versus Bengaluru Rs16.1-17.8L; PhysicsWallah (Noida) growth manager Rs9.7-14.0L at 3-4yrs (3 salaries, AmbitionBox low confidence). Levels.fyi's Hyderabad marketing median of Rs9.03L versus Bengaluru Rs19.83L supports a material discount. In practice the credible employers here are Chennai SaaS (Freshworks, Zoho, Chargebee), Hyderabad (Darwinbox), Pune and Ahmedabad D2C. ESOP terms usually match the metro row; the cut is in fixed cash.

This row is strongly bimodal and the single number is misleading unless you split it. LOW MODE - media/creative agencies and IT services (GroupM/WPP Media, Publicis, Omnicom, Accenture, Infosys): AmbitionBox shows WPP Media performance marketing manager Rs7.1-10.5L across 23 salaries, Publicis Media/Publicis Global Delivery performance marketing analyst Rs6.0L at 3yrs, Accenture digital marketing associate Rs4.8L at 2yrs. Entry-level here is Rs5.5-8L fixed with little or no equity and a 5-10% variable. HIGH MODE - listed/late-stage consumer internet and global tech (Swiggy, Eternal/Zomato, Meesho, Amazon, Nykaa): Swiggy growth manager 1-3yr Rs17.4-25.9L (overall Rs20.5-23.6L across 48 salaries, AmbitionBox high confidence), Meesho growth manager 3-6yr Rs37.7-44.4L, Amazon performance marketing associate Rs12.6L at 3yrs, Lenskart performance marketing manager 3-6yr Rs16.6-18.4L. Levels.fyi India Marketing (verified offers, updated 10 Sep 2026): median total comp Rs16.44L, 25th percentile Rs9.38L, 75th Rs26.58L, with Bengaluru at Rs19.83L, Mumbai Rs13.79L, Gurgaon Rs11.56L. Total-high of Rs26L reflects the high mode with RSUs plus a 10-15% cash bonus. If the offer in front of you is from an agency, benchmark against the low mode only.

The best-sourced non-metro row, because large employers report at volume in tier-2. AmbitionBox (Sep 2026, 47.9k salaries): Digital Marketing Executive 0-1yr Rs2.5-2.8L and 1-3yr Rs2.9-3.2L nationally, with Pune Rs3.2-3.5L, Hyderabad Rs3.3-3.7L, Chennai-area comparable; Digital Marketing Specialist 1-3yr Rs3.9-4.4L nationally with Chennai Rs5.4-5.9L and Pune Rs6.3-6.9L on the blended average; Marketing Associate Pune Rs5.3-6.0L. Indeed India: Digital Marketing Executive average base Rs2.28L (588 salaries, 25 May 2026) with Bengaluru Rs3.85L, Pune Rs3.79L, Hyderabad Rs3.61L; the Marketing Executive page (2.4k salaries, 30 Jun 2026) gives a Rs1.28L-Rs4.19L spread. The Rs12L top of the band is captured by global-capability-centre roles such as Amazon Hyderabad or Chennai SaaS, not by domestic firms. Levels.fyi Hyderabad marketing median Rs9.03L (all levels) supports that upper tail. Equity is RSU-based at MNCs and near-zero at domestic large employers; variable is typically 5-10%.

salary_benchmarks.family: Management trainee and graduate leadership programmes (India, 0-2 years experience) — business-side/non-engineering entry-level: MT, GET-equivalent business tracks, graduate leadership/rotational programmes, founder's office & chief-of-staff associate, business/growth associate, entry-level business analyst

bands.note: Seed companies almost never run a named 'management trainee programme'; the equivalent is a founder's office / chief-of-staff / business-associate hire. Anchors: letsenterprise.in puts early-stage startup freshers at Rs 3-5 LPA and non-tech freshers at Rs 3-5 LPA standard with good companies at Rs 8-10 LPA; Beyond Campus (2026) puts founder's-office freshers at Rs 6-12 LPA for Series A-C, so seed sits at the bottom of that; Internshala's live founder's-office/CoS fresher listings for 2025-26 grads run Rs 9,975 to Rs 98,881 per month (Rs 1.2L to Rs 11.9L annualised), confirming a very long right tail from a handful of well-funded repeat-founder companies. Fixed high of 9 is the realistic ceiling for a non-IIM/non-IIT candidate; 10-12 LPA fixed exists but only at Peak XV/Accel-seeded companies hiring off tier-1 campuses. Variable is usually nil or token at this stage. Total-comp high of 14 is fixed 9 plus roughly Rs 4-5L/yr of paper ESOP (seed pools are 8-12 percent fully diluted; a junior grant is 0.05-0.15 percent vesting over 4 years) — treat that ESOP as lottery-ticket value, not cash, and do not accept a fixed-cash discount for it. Confidence medium: the stage-specific India numbers come from two or three sources rather than a large panel.

Genuinely thin data — no source I found reports seed-stage, non-metro, business-side entry pay directly. This row is an extrapolation, flagged as such. Construction: the metro seed band (4.5-9 fixed) discounted by the 15-30 percent tier-1-to-tier-2 gap that multiple India city-comparison sources report, floored by the broad-market Indian management-trainee baseline — Indeed India shows an all-India MT average of Rs 37,087/month (Rs 4.45 LPA) with a floor of Rs 18,147/month (Rs 2.18 LPA) across 125 salaries updated 29 July 2026, and PayScale India shows entry-level (under 1 year) Manager Trainee average total comp of Rs 4,41,784 with a 10th-percentile base of Rs 1.93L (92 profiles, updated 23 June 2026). Cross-check: hyring.com puts tier-3 MBA freshers at Rs 3-6 LPA, which is the same population. ESOP at a seed company outside the metros is worth close to nothing on a risk-adjusted basis, so total high is only modestly above fixed high.

Best-evidenced startup row. Beyond Campus (2026) states Rs 6-12 LPA for founder's-office freshers at Series A-C companies, with top-tier startups higher; letsenterprise.in independently puts well-funded growth-stage startup freshers at Rs 5-9 LPA. Glassdoor India cross-checks the metro envelope: Management Trainee in Bangalore averages Rs 7,50,000/yr with a 25th-75th of Rs 5,00,000 to Rs 12,23,750; Gurgaon averages Rs 6,80,000 with 25th-75th of Rs 4,50,000 to Rs 11,90,000. So 6-12 fixed is well supported for Bengaluru and Gurugram; Mumbai runs higher (see the listed/large row). Variable at this stage is typically 5-10 percent of fixed and often paid on company rather than individual targets. Total high of 16 assumes 12 fixed plus about 1 LPA variable plus roughly Rs 3 LPA/yr of ESOP paper value (Series A pools are 12-15 percent; junior grants cluster at 0.05-0.1 percent, per incorpx). Judgement rule: at Series A-B an offer under 6 LPA fixed in these three cities is below market for a graduate business hire regardless of how the ESOP is described.

Extrapolated, not directly measured — I found no source reporting Series A-B business-side entry pay for Pune, Ahmedabad, Jaipur, Indore, Kochi, Chandigarh or Coimbatore specifically. Method: metro Series A-B band (6-12) taken to 70-85 percent, the tier-2-vs-tier-1 ratio that India city-comparison sources report, then sanity-checked against measured non-metro points from Indeed India's MT city table (Pune Rs 64,417/month = Rs 7.73 LPA, Hyderabad Rs 49,422/month = Rs 5.93 LPA, Noida Rs 48,163/month = Rs 5.78 LPA, 125 salaries, 29 July 2026) and against hyring.com's tier-2 MBA fresher band of Rs 6-10 LPA. Caveat: Pune and Hyderabad behave more like metros for funded startups than like true tier-2 cities, so an offer in either can legitimately sit at or slightly above this band's high. Total high assumes fixed 8, modest variable, and thin ESOP.

Late-stage and unicorn business-side graduate hiring. letsenterprise.in puts unicorn/late-stage freshers at Rs 8-12 LPA, which sets the floor and the middle. The upper half comes from Levels.fyi India (filtered to entry-level Business Analyst, last updated 10 September 2026): all-India median total comp Rs 10,84,011 with 25th Rs 7,66,411, 75th Rs 14,91,217, 90th Rs 18,10,000; Greater Bengaluru median Rs 12,26,071 with 25th Rs 7,92,340, 75th Rs 16,48,623, 90th Rs 18,50,000. Important caveat on that source: Levels.fyi's India business-analyst sample skews toward GCCs, big tech and banks (its top-paying employers on that page are Google, Amazon, Flipkart, Citi, Accenture), so it flatters a pure Series C startup MT offer — I used it for the ceiling, not the centre. Variable at Series C+ is typically 10-15 percent and ESOPs are real (buyback programmes exist), worth roughly Rs 2-4 LPA/yr on a junior grant. Total high of 22 is fixed 16 plus variable plus ESOP plus a joining bonus. Confidence medium rather than high because no source measures 'Series C+ non-engineering management trainee' as its own cut.

Sparse. Late-stage startups concentrate business hiring in Bengaluru, Gurugram and Mumbai, so the non-metro population here is mostly city-ops, supply and category roles in Pune, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, Chennai, Jaipur, Lucknow and similar — and those pay materially below HQ-based analyst roles. Construction: unicorn/late-stage fresher band of Rs 8-12 LPA (letsenterprise.in) discounted 15-25 percent for location, floored by Levels.fyi's all-India entry-level BA 25th percentile of Rs 7,66,411 and Indeed's non-metro MT points (Hyderabad Rs 5.93 LPA, Noida Rs 5.78 LPA, all-India average Rs 4.45 LPA). Marked low confidence because it is a derived figure, not an observed distribution. If the role is a city-ops or field role rather than an HQ analyst role, expect the bottom of this band plus a large sales/ops incentive component.

This band is deliberately wide because the market is genuinely bimodal, and that split is the single most important thing when judging an offer. Cluster A, the elite graduate leadership programmes recruiting from IIM-ABC/XLRI/ISB: HUL ULIP Rs 22-28 LPA, ITC IBD Rs 20-25 LPA, Nestle/P&G Rs 18-30 LPA, Aditya Birla Group MBA track Rs 8-15 LPA (salaryinsight.in, 2026); Prosple lists Aditya Birla MT at Rs 8-8.5 LPA average. Cluster B, mainstream corporate MT — banking MTs at SBI/HDFC/ICICI Rs 6-12 LPA, manufacturing MTs at Tata Steel/JSW/L&T Rs 8-15 LPA, non-MBA conglomerate MTs Rs 5-10 LPA. Glassdoor India measures the blended distribution: all-India MT average total pay Rs 7,25,000 with 25th Rs 4,67,500 and 75th Rs 11,00,000; Mumbai average Rs 10,00,000 with 25th-75th of Rs 6,00,000 to Rs 15,12,500; Bangalore average Rs 7,50,000 with 25th-75th of Rs 5,00,000 to Rs 12,23,750. 6figr shows Mumbai MT averaging about Rs 13 LPA, but that sample skews to people well past the 0-2 year mark, so treat it as an upper reference only. Fixed high of 18 reflects that a Rs 22-28 LPA elite-programme CTC is typically Rs 16-20 LPA fixed once variable, retention and one-time components are stripped out; total high of 30 is the top of the P&G/Nestle range. Michael Page's India Salary Guide 2026 puts increments at 8-12 percent, so year-two progression from any of these anchors is modest. High confidence: four or more independent sources agree on the shape and the levels.

The largest population in this whole family by headcount — BPO/ITES and shared-services MT programmes, bank probationary/MT cadres, and manufacturing MT postings at plant towns. Low end: Genpact Management Trainee, whose India footprint is heavily Hyderabad, Kolkata and Jaipur, reports Rs 3.6-6.7 LPA on AmbitionBox and Rs 5,35,000-11,12,500 (25th-75th) on Glassdoor across 1,616 submissions, with Indeed at about Rs 6.46 LPA. Broad market: Indeed India MT average Rs 37,087/month (Rs 4.45 LPA), range Rs 18,147-75,792/month (Rs 2.18-9.09 LPA), 125 salaries updated 29 July 2026; PayScale India Manager Trainee entry-level (under 1 year) average total comp Rs 4,41,784 and early-career (1-4 years) Rs 4,76,017, 92 profiles updated 23 June 2026. High end: manufacturing MT programmes at Tata Steel, JSW and L&T sit at Rs 8-15 LPA (salaryinsight.in) and are located at Jamshedpur, Vijayanagar and similar non-metro sites, which is why fixed high is 12 rather than 8. Reality check on expectations from Naukri JobSpeak 2026: 73 percent of Indian undergraduates expect above Rs 5 LPA but only 40 percent actually receive an offer at that level — so a Rs 4.5-5 LPA MT offer outside the metros is at or slightly above median, not a lowball. ESOP is not part of the package in this row; total high of 16 is fixed plus performance bonus and shift/location allowances.

salary_benchmarks.family: Product analyst and associate product manager (APM) — entry level, 0–2 years, India

bands.note: Widest band in the table because seed pay is founder-dependent, not market-set. Live Wellfound postings in Bengaluru/Gurugram show the real spread: APM Bengaluru Rs 4.5-6L and Rs 5-8L (remote India) at the bottom, PM roles at Rs 3-6L in HSR Layout, up to 'Associate Product Manager (Technical)' Bengaluru at Rs 12-18L and a Gurgaon technical PM at Rs 14-24L with 0.1-1.0% equity. Fixed low of 6 is a product-analyst/APM-generalist offer at an unbranded seed company; 14 is a well-funded seed (Accel/Blume/Peak XV pre-A) hiring an IIT/IIM or ex-APM-program candidate. Variable pay is usually zero at this stage. Total high of 18 = Rs 14L fixed plus notional ESOP only: typical grant 0.05-0.30% on a Rs 40-100 Cr post-money, i.e. roughly Rs 2-8L of paper value spread over a 4-year vest with a 1-year cliff, so about Rs 1-4L/yr notional and realistically worth zero. Do not treat the ESOP as cash when judging an offer here. Confidence medium not high: postings are real and current but few seed companies report CTC to AmbitionBox/Glassdoor, so there is no large-sample check on this band. Within the band, product analyst titles sit in the bottom third (6-9) and APM titles in the top half (10-14).

This is the weakest cell in the table and I am openly extrapolating. There is no stage-tagged salary dataset for seed startups in Pune, Hyderabad, Chennai, Ahmedabad, Indore, Jaipur, Kochi or Kolkata — the sample sizes collapse (AmbitionBox has 63 product-analyst salaries for all of Pune, 92 APM salaries for all of Ahmedabad). What I anchored on: AmbitionBox product analyst Pune typical band Rs 8.9-11L with a 1-3 yr average of only Rs 6.7L, AmbitionBox APM Ahmedabad 1-3 yrs average Rs 11.2L (but that pool is dominated by mid-size product/services firms, not seed startups), Cutshort's model showing PM pay in Ahmedabad Rs 13.6L, Coimbatore Rs 12.8L and Bhubaneswar Rs 12L versus Rs 20L in Bengaluru, and Wellfound's remote-India APM postings at Rs 5-8L. I applied roughly a 30-35% discount to the metro seed band. Treat 4.5-9 as an educated bracket, not a benchmark. Variable is essentially nil; ESOP at a non-metro seed company is worth even less in practice, so total high of 11 is 9 fixed plus about 2 of notional paper.

Anchors that converge here: AmbitionBox APM India 1-3 yrs average Rs 13.1L (15.5k salaries, updated 6 Sep 2026); Cutshort's startup-focused calculator for a 2-year PM gives minimum Rs 9.9L, average Rs 15.2L, top paymasters Rs 24.3L; Levels.fyi entry-level PM India 25th percentile Rs 9.97L and median Rs 15.69L (updated 10 Sep 2026); Glassdoor Bengaluru APM 25th percentile Rs 11.94L. Real Series A/B postings scraped from AmbitionBox jobs: Jar (Series B fintech, Bengaluru, 1-3 yrs) Rs 16.3-22.2L, and Wellfound's Bengaluru 'APM (Technical)' at Rs 12-18L. Fixed low of 9 is a product analyst at a Series A B2B SaaS company; 18 is an APM at a hot Series B consumer/fintech company hiring against big-tech offers. Variable typically 5-10% of CTC at this stage. ESOP is normal and meaningful here: 0.02-0.10%, commonly quoted as Rs 8-20L of paper over 4 years, i.e. Rs 2-5L/yr. Total high of 24 = 18 fixed + ~1.5 variable + ~4.5 annualised ESOP. Confidence medium rather than high because the underlying role-level data is well sampled but the funding-stage attribution is my mapping from company names, not a published stage cut.

Low confidence because almost no Series A-B product org outside the three metros reports enough entry-level data to benchmark. The usable signals: AmbitionBox APM Pune 1-3 yrs average Rs 11.4L and APM Ahmedabad 1-3 yrs average Rs 11.2L, both against a national APM 1-3 yrs average of Rs 13.1L — a roughly 13-15% non-metro discount; AmbitionBox product analyst Pune 1-3 yrs average Rs 6.7L against Rs 10.4L nationally, a much steeper discount for the analyst title; Indeed India APM city medians of Hyderabad Rs 13.0L, Chennai Rs 13.0L and Noida Rs 12.5L versus Gurgaon Rs 20.1L. Note that Hyderabad and Pune behave almost like metros (their AmbitionBox APM averages, Rs 16.2L and Rs 16.1L across all experience, actually match Bengaluru's Rs 16.5L), while genuine tier-2 cities sit 30-40% lower. If the offer you are judging is in Hyderabad or Pune, use the metro Series A-B row and shave 10%; use this row for Indore, Jaipur, Kochi, Coimbatore, Kolkata, Bhubaneswar and similar. Total high of 17 = 13 fixed + ~1 variable + ~3 annualised ESOP.

The best-evidenced row: five independent datasets land on the same 12-22 fixed window for a growth-stage/unicorn APM in a metro. Levels.fyi entry-level PM India (updated 10 Sep 2026): p25 Rs 9.97L, median Rs 15.69L, p75 Rs 20.07L, p90 Rs 32.6L. Glassdoor Bengaluru APM (1,299 salaries, Jul 2026): p25 Rs 11.94L, median total Rs 17.0L, p75 Rs 21.8L, p90 Rs 26.9L. Indeed India APM (Aug 2026): average Rs 16.4L, range Rs 11.7-22.9L, Bengaluru Rs 17.0L, Gurgaon Rs 20.1L. Cutshort 2-yr PM top paymasters Rs 24.3L. AmbitionBox company rows at this stage: Meesho Rs 12.9-18.7L, Rupeek (Bengaluru, 1-3 yrs posting) Rs 14-19.1L, HighRadius Rs 16.8-19.8L, Sprinklr Rs 20.8-23.4L, ShareChat Rs 26.4-30L, MakeMyTrip Rs 26.4-29.7L; Indeed lists slice at Rs 22.0L and Acko at Rs 21.3L. Fixed low of 12 is a product analyst at a Series C consumer company; 22 is a structured APM-programme hire (Flipkart/PhonePe/Zepto/Razorpay tier). Variable 10-15% is standard. ESOP is a real component at this stage: Rs 15-35L of grant value over 4 years, i.e. Rs 4-9L/yr, and at a late-stage company with buyback history it is partly liquid. Total high of 32 = 22 fixed + ~3 variable + ~7 annualised ESOP, which matches Levels.fyi's p90 of Rs 32.6L.

Most Series C+ Indian product companies keep product roles in Bengaluru/Gurugram/Mumbai, so this row covers a genuinely thin population — mainly Hyderabad and Pune offices (Sprinklr, Darwinbox, Highradius, Zeta, Icertis, Mindtickle) plus Chennai (Zoho, Freshworks, Chargebee). Anchors: AmbitionBox APM Hyderabad all-experience average Rs 16.2L and Pune Rs 16.1L, essentially matching Bengaluru's Rs 16.5L, but AmbitionBox APM Pune 1-3 yrs average is only Rs 11.4L; AmbitionBox product analyst Hyderabad band Rs 9.9-13.1L; Indeed India APM Hyderabad Rs 13.0L and Chennai Rs 13.0L; Levels.fyi shows Hyderabad (Rs 45.1L) and Pune (Rs 35.4L) PM medians close to Bengaluru's Rs 46.1L at all levels. So the discount to metro is real but modest, roughly 15-25% at entry level. If the company is in a true tier-2 city, drop to the Series A-B other-city row instead. Variable 10-12%; ESOP norms are the same as the metro Series C+ row but grants tend to be one notch smaller. Total high of 24 = 17 fixed + ~2 variable + ~5 annualised ESOP.

Deliberately the widest fixed band because this category is bimodal and a single midpoint would mislead. Lower mode — Indian IT services, BFSI, listed non-tech and domestic internet: AmbitionBox shows TCS APM Rs 7.3-9.1L, Cognizant product analyst Rs 4.6-5.1L, Paytm APM Rs 10.8-12.6L, Kapture CX Rs 12.9-14.4L, GEP Worldwide Rs 13.4-18.4L, and a live Morningstar Mumbai posting (2-5 yrs) at Rs 8.5-12L; AmbitionBox's IT Services industry cut for product analyst is Rs 8.8-10.2L. Upper mode — global product MNCs and GCCs: American Express APM Rs 17-20L, Target product analyst Rs 12.9-14.7L, Sprinklr product analyst Rs 16.4-23.7L, HCA Healthcare Rs 16.7-24.5L, and AmbitionBox names Walmart as top-paying APM at Rs 31.7L. Levels.fyi entry-level PM India p90 is Rs 32.6L. Fixed high of 24 is a strong MNC/GCC entry offer; a Google APM1 or Uber/Walmart APM sits above this table entirely and is a rare campus-programme outcome, not a benchmark. Variable/bonus 10-20% is standard here, and RSUs (real, liquid stock) rather than illiquid ESOPs are common at the MNC end, worth roughly Rs 5-10L/yr at entry level. Total high of 36 = 24 fixed + ~3 bonus + ~9 RSU. Confidence medium: role-level sampling is excellent, but the two modes are so far apart that any single band overstates precision. Judge an offer against the correct sub-mode, not against the midpoint.

Same bimodality as the metro listed/large row, shifted down. Lower mode is Indian IT services and listed non-tech in Pune, Chennai, Kolkata, Coimbatore and Ahmedabad: AmbitionBox Cognizant product analyst Rs 4.6-5.1L, Zeomega Infotech Rs 8.6-9.9L, TCS APM Rs 7.3-9.1L, AmbitionBox product analyst Pune typical band Rs 8.9-11L with a 1-3 yrs average of only Rs 6.7L, APM Ahmedabad typical Rs 11.6-14.2L with 1-3 yrs average Rs 11.2L. Upper mode is MNC GCCs, concentrated in Hyderabad, Pune and Chennai: AmbitionBox Target product analyst Rs 12.9-14.7L, HCA Healthcare Rs 16.7-24.5L (Hyderabad-heavy), and Indeed's Hyderabad APM median Rs 13.0L, Chennai Rs 13.0L, Noida Rs 12.5L. Indeed's product analyst city medians for Chennai (Rs 10.1L) and Hyderabad (Rs 7.4L) sit near the bottom of this band, though on only 23 reported salaries so treat them as weak. Variable 10-15%; RSUs exist only at the MNC/GCC end. Total high of 24 = 16 fixed + ~2.5 bonus + ~5.5 RSU. Caveat on the whole table: AmbitionBox and Glassdoor figures are self-reported CTC and skew high; Indeed India sample sizes are tiny (23-25 salaries); 6figr.com renders its numbers in JavaScript and Glassdoor and AmbitionBox metro city pages returned 403 to direct fetches, so those were used only via indexed search snippets or not at all. Levels.fyi India PM data is heavily big-tech weighted (all-levels median Rs 44.6L) and should never be used as an entry-level anchor except via its explicit entry-level cut.

salary_benchmarks.family: Business development, inside sales and account management (entry-level, 0-2 years, India)

bands.note: Live Wellfound India listings (read 10 Sep 2026) tagged 'Early Stage Startup' show SDR in Gurugram at Rs 4-6L (1 yr exp), Sales Associate / Account Manager in Bengaluru at Rs 5-8L (0 yrs), and BD Associate Bengaluru at Rs 5.5-8L (1 yr). AmbitionBox 0-1 yr averages for the unbranded pool that seed startups hire from: BDE Rs 3.3-3.6L (16.5k salaries), Inside Sales Exec Rs 3.5-3.8L, BD Associate Rs 4.4-4.9L. The Rs 7L top of the fixed band is a funded seed B2B SaaS hiring its first SDRs against Series-A competition; Rs 3.5L is an SMB/agency BDE role with the same title. Total-comp high assumes ~Rs 2L of incentive at 100% quota (70:30 to 80:20 fixed:variable is the Indian SDR norm) and treats ESOP as near-zero in cash terms: entry-level junior grants at seed are typically 0.05-0.1% of a 7-10% pool, illiquid, and should not be counted when judging an offer. Confidence medium not high because no salary aggregator tags employers by funding stage - this row is built from stage-labelled job postings plus the broad 0-1 yr AmbitionBox pool.

Weakest cell in the table - almost no source tags both funding stage and non-metro city. Built by applying the observed metro-to-tier-2 discount to the seed metro row. Indeed India monthly base for BDE (Sep 2026): all-India Rs 20,811/mo = ~Rs 2.5L/yr (2.9k salaries), vs Bengaluru Rs 37,133/mo = ~Rs 4.5L/yr; tier-2 sits between - Jaipur Rs 28,323/mo (~Rs 3.4L), Indore Rs 28,881/mo (~Rs 3.5L), Ahmedabad Rs 24,361/mo (~Rs 2.9L). talent.com (10,000 India postings, Sep 2026) puts BDE entry-level starting pay at Rs 3.25L and the national median at Rs 3.3L. Wellfound early-stage postings outside the three metros: inside sales Pune Rs 4-9L (1 yr), inside sales Kochi Rs 4-6L (2 yrs). Note Pune, Hyderabad and Chennai are 'other Indian city' by this table's definition but pay far closer to metro rates than Jaipur or Indore - treat Rs 5L as the tech-hub top and Rs 2.5-3.5L as genuine tier-2/3. Total high assumes incentive only; seed ESOP outside metros is rarely material.

AmbitionBox SDR India 0-1 yr sits at Rs 5.7-6.2L and 1-3 yrs at Rs 7.0-7.7L (updated Sep 2026); Bengaluru SDR averages Rs 8.8-9.7L and Gurugram Rs 8.7-9.9L across all experience, so a 0-2 yr rep in those cities lands in the high-5s to 9s fixed. PayScale entry-level SDR in Bangalore: average Rs 4.5L, base range Rs 2.53-9.86L, total Rs 3.56-10L. Glassdoor India BDR (484 salaries, Jan 2026) 25th percentile total pay Rs 7.22L - roughly where a Series A-B rep starts. Wellfound Bengaluru startup postings for 0-1 yr sales/AM roles cluster Rs 5-8L. Series A-B typically pays 15-25% under a Series C+ SaaS for the same seat and closes the gap with a larger ESOP grant; total-comp high of Rs 13L assumes Rs 9L fixed + ~Rs 3L variable at full attainment + ~Rs 1L/yr of notional vesting ESOP. Discount the ESOP heavily unless there is a buyback history. This is a B2B-SaaS-flavoured band; a consumer or D2C Series A will pay closer to the seed row.

Extrapolated, not directly measured - no source segments Series A-B employers by city. Anchors used: AmbitionBox SDR city averages show Hyderabad Rs 7.8-8.8L (253 salaries) and Pune Rs 8.6-9.6L against Bengaluru Rs 8.8-9.7L, i.e. only a 2-11% discount in the tech hubs; AmbitionBox Inside Sales Specialist 0-1 yr is Rs 4.0-4.4L nationally and Inside Sales Exec 0-1 yr Rs 3.5-3.8L. Indeed tier-2 BDE base runs Rs 2.9-3.5L/yr against Rs 4.5L in Bengaluru, a 25-35% haircut. So the honest read is a split market: a Series A-B SaaS SDR seat in Pune, Hyderabad or Chennai realistically pays Rs 5.5-6.5L fixed, while the same title in Jaipur, Indore, Coimbatore or Ahmedabad pays Rs 3.5-4.5L. Total high of Rs 9L = Rs 6.5L fixed + ~Rs 2L variable + small ESOP. Treat this row as a planning estimate, not a benchmark.

Best single anchor: LeadSquared (Series C, Bengaluru) SDR 0-1 yr Rs 6.1-7.2L (18 salaries) and 1-3 yrs Rs 6.3-7.9L (39 salaries), page-level high confidence, Apr 2026. Higher-paying late-stage comparables, all AmbitionBox and all thin-sample so treat as the top of the range not the middle: MoEngage SDR 0-3 yrs Rs 8.4-11.6L (n=5), Rippling India SDR 1-5 yrs Rs 12.1-15.2L (n=19, Aug 2026), Whatfix SDR 0-3 yrs Rs 11.6-17L (n=5), Darwinbox SDR 1-3 yrs Rs 12.4-14.9L (n=8), Chargebee SDR Rs 9.6-14.2L (n=4). Glassdoor India BDR: median total Rs 11.8L, 25th Rs 7.22L, 75th Rs 17L, base roughly Rs 6-12L (484 salaries, Jan 2026). Levels.fyi India 'Business Development' 25th percentile total comp Rs 8.45L, median Rs 13.73L (all levels, updated 10 Sep 2026). Total-comp high of Rs 18L = Rs 12L fixed + ~Rs 4L variable at quota + ~Rs 2L/yr vesting ESOP, which at Series C+ is genuinely worth something and sometimes has a buyback. Confidence capped at medium because only LeadSquared has a real 0-2 yr sample; the rest are single-digit-n or span wider experience.

Extrapolated from role-level city data rather than stage-tagged data. AmbitionBox SDR by city (Sep 2026): Bengaluru Rs 8.8-9.7L, Gurugram Rs 8.7-9.9L, New Delhi Rs 8.9-10.1L, Pune Rs 8.6-9.6L (231 salaries), Hyderabad Rs 7.8-8.8L (253 salaries) - so Pune and Hyderabad, which are 'other Indian city' here, run only about 2-11% below the metros, and Hyderabad hosts genuinely large Series C+ GTM floors (Darwinbox, MoEngage have Hyderabad/Bengaluru presence). Chennai carries Freshworks and Zoho. True tier-2 cities (Jaipur, Indore, Kochi, Ahmedabad, Coimbatore) essentially do not host Series C+ SaaS SDR teams, so the low end of this row reflects support-hub inside-sales seats rather than quota-carrying SDRs. Randstad's 2025-26 salary trends report notes Bengaluru leads junior-level pay nationally at Rs 7.16L average across sectors, with Tier-2 catching up mainly at senior levels, not junior.
